name: עֻזָּא
summary: Above all Uzzah son of Abinadab, who drove the new cart carrying the ark of God and put out his hand to hold it when the oxen stumbled, and “God struck him there for the error, and he died there by the ark of God”; David called the place Perez-uzzah (2Sa 6:3–8; 1Ch 13:7–11). The name, spelled עֻזָּא or עֻזָּה, is also borne by a Merarite Levite (1Ch 6:14), a Benjamite son of Ehud (1Ch 8:7), and the head of a family of temple servants who returned from exile (Ezr 2:49; Neh 7:51); “the garden of Uzza” was the burial place of Manasseh and Amon (2Ki 21:18, 26). The name is a short form of עֹז “strength”, perhaps of a longer name such as עֻזִּיָּהוּ; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “וְעֻזָּא and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.”
“Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled; and the anger of Yahweh burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there.”
“He called that place פֶּרֶץ עֻזָּה to this day.”
“Because you did not carry it the first time, Yahweh our God broke out against us, because we did not seek him according to the ordinance.”
A Merarite: “Shimei his son, עֻזָּה his son.”
A Benjamite: “he fathered עֻזָּא and Ahihud.”
“The sons of עֻזָּא”, among the temple servants; so Neh 7:51.
The place: “in the garden of Uzza”; so 2Ki 21:26.

note: BDB's p.bx.ag and p.bx.ah list the same 16 tokens (עֻזָּא and עֻזָּה); both keys are named here so neither is left unassigned; the uses should be counted once. TIPNR's Uzzah@1Ch.6.29 is 1Ch 6:14 in the Hebrew numbering. The garden of Uzza (2Ki 21:18, 26) is a place (TIPNR Uzza@2Ki.21.18) and is not tagged. The meaning “strength” takes the name as עֹז with the ending ־ָא, as Aramaic-shaped short names; whether it is short for Uzziah or Uzziel is not shown.
